criteria.note: The WorkerSpawner start seam is filled by a REAL worktree-isolated in-session start. WorktreeInSessionStart.__call__(worker_id, env) provisions a git-worktree-isolated workspace via WorktreeProvisioner.add (an in-line `git worktree add --detach`), dispatches the worker through the injected in-session callback self._dispatch(worker_id, env, worktree), and returns a retireable handle {worker_id, worktree, worker}. make_worktree_in_session_spawner reuses make_in_session_spawner / AccountSpreader (one account per worker, no second account or handle implementation) and wires starter.stop as the InSessionSpawner stop, so retire stops the worker cooperatively (dispatch_stop) and removes the worktree (WorktreeProvisioner.remove) and releases the account. InSessionSpawner._assemble_env threads the selected account's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR into env, so the worker reuses that account's login. The worker dies with the session (in-session dispatch, nothing detached). Gate-tested with a fake provisioner (_FakeWorktree) and fake dispatch: worktree-per-worker provision + in-session dispatch carrying CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/scope/worktree, retireable handle (stop + worktree removed), and a full launcher run scaling to the account count one-account-per-worker then draining and removing every worktree.

It NEVER spawns a detached, headless, or background process. I enumerated every subprocess/os call in the whole spawn path (FleetLauncher.reconcile -> InSessionSpawner.spawn -> _assemble_env -> ACCT.resolve -> WorktreeInSessionStart.__call__ -> WorktreeProvisioner.add/_git_worktree -> self._dispatch -> retire -> stop): (1) fleet.py _git_worktree runs subprocess.run(['git','worktree', ...]) only, a synchronous in-line git call (add --detach, remove --force), with subprocess imported LAZILY inside the helper (never at module top); (2) accounts.py accounts_root runs subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','--git-common-dir']), a pre-existing synchronous git call to locate the shared runs root, not a worker and not touched by this commit; (3) the worker launch itself is the injected self._dispatch(worker_id, env, worktree) seam, not a process this module starts. A full-diff grep across all 20 files finds no Popen, os.fork/forkpty, os.exec, os.spawn/posix_spawn, os.system, setsid, nohup, start_new_session, creationflags, multiprocessing, pty.spawn, systemd, crontab, or background `claude -p` in any executable path (the only such tokens are in prose describing the ban and in the selftest's own mutation strings). fleet.py's os.* uses are os.environ/os.path/os.makedirs (filesystem only). With no dispatch wired the module holds the same fail-loud boundary it held as a reference.

The no-detach boundary has REAL teeth. selftest _no_detached_worker_spawn(src) checks the shipped fleet.py source against _DETACH_TOKENS (Popen, os.fork/forkpty, os.exec, os.spawn/posix_spawn, os.system, setsid, nohup, start_new_session, creationflags, multiprocessing, pty.spawn, claude -p). I independently proved the teeth are non-vacuous by injecting a detached spawn into fleet.py's spawn path (unreachable statement in WorktreeInSessionStart.__call__ so no rogue process actually ran) two ways: (a) subprocess.Popen(['claude','-p','x'], start_new_session=True) -> selftest 1486 passed, 2 failed (the no-detach teeth and the only-external-program assertion both RED); (b) os.system('claude -p work &') -> selftest 1487 passed, 1 failed (the no-detach teeth RED). After each mutation a git checkout restored .warp/fleet.py, git diff --quiet .warp/fleet.py was clean, and the fleet.py sha256 returned to the committed 143aa3c2..., with the gate back to 1488/0. The launcher control logic (elastic scaling, one-account-per-worker via AccountSpreader, retire releasing the account) stays gate-tested via the fake spawner; the live in-session start is a reference path, not gate-run.

It FAILS LOUD where no in-session mechanism is wired, and never leaks a worktree. WorktreeInSessionStart.__call__ checks dispatch None BEFORE provisioning, delegating to in_session_start which raises SpawnPrimitiveError with no worktree added; a dispatch returning None removes the provisioned worktree then raises SpawnPrimitiveError (no fabricated handle); a dispatch that raises removes the worktree and re-raises. All three are gate-tested and green (no leaked worktree in any). The cmd_fleet default in bin/warp keeps start = fleet.in_session_start (the fail-loud reference), so a bare `warp fleet` with no in-session start wired stops at the first spawn rather than auto-detaching (bin/warp untouched by this commit). The coordinator drive is documented in docs/runbook.md: workers are in-session, git-worktree-isolated, opt-in, one account per worker (never one account as two workers), agent-mediated at launch, die with the session, and fail loud where no in-session mechanism exists.

findings.text: Non-blocking. The live worktree-isolated in-session start is a REFERENCE edge, agent-mediated at runtime (the coordinator injects dispatch(worker_id, env, worktree)) and NOT gate-run; the gate drives a fake provisioner and a fake dispatch. This is disclosed honestly (capabilities.yaml worker_in_session_start status: reference) and is the correct fill, not a shortcut: a pure-Python spawn could only launch an in-session worker by detaching, which is forbidden (feedback_no_rogue_processes, PLAN-0007 NG1), so shipping the seam plus reference plus documented coordinator procedure plus teeth is the architecturally correct choice (RULE #6).

Non-blocking. The os.system mutation trips the general _no_detached_worker_spawn teeth (RED, 1 failure) but not the separate 'only external program is git worktree' assertion, because that assertion keys on Popen and the git-worktree/dispatch presence; the subprocess.Popen mutation trips both (2 failures). Either mutation being caught is sufficient - a detached spawn cannot slip past the gate - so this is coverage detail, not a gap.

summary: WARP-1010 (real in-session worker spawner - fill the fleet spawn seam in-session, never detached, standalone) passes with notes at 67731d29, zero blocking findings. This is the most safety-sensitive fleet change and the no-detach bright line HOLDS. AC1: WorktreeInSessionStart fills the WorkerSpawner start seam with a git-worktree-isolated in-session start that provisions a worktree per worker (in-line git only), dispatches the worker through an injected in-session callback, returns a retireable handle, and retires by stopping the worker cooperatively and removing the worktree, reusing AccountSpreader one-account-per-worker with the account's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR threaded in. AC2: the spawn path spawns NO detached/headless/background process - every subprocess/os call enumerated is either a synchronous in-line git call (git worktree in fleet.py, git rev-parse in the pre-existing accounts.py) or the injected dispatch seam, with subprocess imported lazily and no Popen/fork/exec/spawn/system/setsid/nohup/start_new_session/multiprocessing/pty/systemd/crontab/background-claude-p anywhere. AC3: the teeth are real - I independently injected a detached subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True) and a background os.system('claude -p work &') into the spawn path and each turned the WARP-1010 no-detach selftest RED (1486/2 and 1487/1), then reverted clean (git diff --quiet, sha256 143aa3c2..., gate 1488/0). AC4: with no in-session dispatch wired the primitive fails loud by name (SpawnPrimitiveError), never fabricates a handle, never detaches, and leaks no worktree (removed on a failed or empty or raising dispatch); the cmd_fleet default stays fail-loud in_session_start. AC5: capabilities.yaml is honest (worker_spawner mechanical, worker_in_session_start reference), the gate is GREEN at R (selftest 1488/0, catalog 5/18/0/0), fleet.py and capabilities.yaml are byte-identical across all eight copies (template sync + pack drift pass), no protected path is touched, and RULE #1 is clean. The manifest binds to R, is standalone, and its proof_digest recomputes to sha256:a5cc12b21d5e2784, matching this verdict. Two non-blocking notes (the live start is a reference edge not gate-run, by correct design; and mutation-coverage detail), both by design. Verdict: pass_with_notes.
